newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, U.S. reach accord on agricultural trade.
newsitem.headline: Israel, U.S. reach accord on agricultural trade.

text.p: Israel's Industry and Trade Ministry said on Tuesday it had reached an agreement with the United States concerning imports of agricultural products and processed foods over the next five years.
The agreement will benefit U.S. agricultural exports to Israel in varying levels, depending on the product.

The Israeli ministry noted that the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) prohibits quotas but allows customs duties to replace quotas. Such tariffs, however, are not allowed under the Free Trade Area Agreement between Israel and the United States.
The U.S. government had demanded, therefore, that Israel, lift all barriers to agricultural imports.
Under the agreement reached between the two countries, Israel will remove all trade barriers for one list of products, including most grains and many processed food products.

A second list consists of products that will be exempt from duties on a limited quantity. This list includes certain milk products, cheeses, certain fresh and frozen fruits and vegetables, canned goods and juices.
The third list of products will be subject to import fees that will gradually be reduced.
Israeli exports will also benefit from improved conditions for those products on which the United States still imposes barriers.
